0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part J ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Inst.tutton on 28 November 1983. after the draft finalized by the Hydraulic Gates and Valves Sectional Committee had been approved by the 0,,1 Engineering DIvision Council.
0.2 Almost every river valley project has
3

reservoir or diversion work for

the control of floods or to store water for Irrigation and power generation or for both. and a spillway with spillway gates for release of flood waters dunng monsoons. Controlled releases of water are also affected by controlled gate, provided in conduits m the body of the dam and tunnels. One method of providing such control in spillways and conduits IS by radial gates. 0.3 This standard is being published in three parts. Part I deals With inspection, testing and assembly at the manufacturing stage. Part 2 deals WIth inspection. testing and assembly at the time of erection and Part 3 deals with mspecuon, testmg and mamtenance after erection. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied With, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance WIth IS : 2-1960'. The number of sigruficant places retained In the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value m this standard.

2.2 General Inspection
2.2.1 It shall be ascertained that the gate parts received at erection site bave been manufactured according to the design and have necessary markmgs of shop inspecnon wherever prescribed. It Shall be ensured that all exposed surfaces of embedded par" have been protected by paintmg, greasing, etc, as specified, The surlaces of embedded parts in contact with concrete shall be free from grease, pamt, etc, for better bonding with concrete. A coatmg of cement wash/cement latex may be apphed, If necessary.

2.2.2 Dimensional differences, If any, shall be accounted for before erection and the drawings corrected accordingly. For erecnon the cnncal dimensions shall be worked out from the drawings. 2.2.3 The reference/centre lmes of piers and bays. and levels having relation, to completed CIVIl structure shall be established at site so as to facihtate erection at proper locations
2.2.4 It shall be ensured that the vanous components of the hoisting arrangement, such as motors, reducnon gear assembly, switches, wire ropes, etc, are provided according to manufacturer's mstructions and erected according to hoist supplier's approved drawings. 2.2.5 The permissible tolerances for embedded parts and components of gate sball be m accordance with Appendix F of IS : 4623-1979',

2.8 IlISpectlon of Complete Gate Inslallation aod Hoists Ioeludlog Electrical Items 2.8.1 Visual inspection of all gates and heists shall be carried out after erection. 2.8.2 Tbe erection tolerance shall be checked for all parts during and after erection 2.8.3 In case of hoists, the following pomts which are by no means exhaustive, need be looked mto by engineer-in-charge: a) Connecuons like sbaft couplings, connections of wire ropes to the drum and gate. connection of hoist components to the base, etc, have been properly made. b) Intermediate supports for shafts are provided at the required locations to permit free movement of shaft, c) In case of double hoists both the hoists are properly synchronized; d) Tbe ends of wire ropes are properly looped and sufficient 'U' clamps have been provided, e) The rope has been tightly wound over the drum, has no kinks and IS properly !ubncated, f) The wire ropes or chams at both ends of the gate and counterweight ( If provided ) have equal initral tension; g) Electnc installations have been properly earthed; and h) The Iinnt switches have been properly adjusted. 2.8.4 It shall be ensured that tbe gate sill, "all plates and other embedded parts are thoroughly cleaned and no foreign rnaterial rs present. 2.8.5 The hoist provided for operanon of tbe gale should firsI be independently tested" ben II IS not connected to the gate to ensure ItS satisfactory working. 3. TESTING
3.1 The gate shall be tested in a dry condition with hoist duly connected for its smooth working. The gate should be fully closed and fully opened and it should be ensured that there IS no obstruction and no undue efforts required for its operation. [f the gate IS not gomg down of Its own weight or found tight in some position, reasons should be mvesngated and remedied instead of forcing .he gate down

3.2 The testing of gate-seals in dry con.liuon should be done by SUItable means, such as by viewmg the contact suuucc against a light source
3.3 In case of rubber seals, water should be poured over the seals so that there WIll not be dry friction of the seals, In case of metal to metal contacts, oil or grease rs to be used. No grease or lubncant is to be used for rubber seals. 3.4 There shall be no noise of friction or any other noise, no signs of excessive friction, no jerky performance, no dug in any posrtion, no dangling of the gate, no twist in rubber seals and rubber seals are not overpressed. 3.5 The gate is to be first kept resnng on srll beam, that is in closed positron. The leakage test can be done III this position by using suuable pump with necessary arrangements of jetting water at 1'5 trmcs the designed pressure on sealing positions from bottom to top All joints if any, shall be tested to ensure perfect working of the gate

3.6 The gate should be fully opened and closed to ensure full opening and
satisfactory closing. The time required for 300 mm open 109 or closing of the gate IS to be recorded.

3.7 The arrangements provided for preventing the travel of the gate or
hoist beyond the designed limit are tested and checked for proper working.
3.8 In case of rope drum hoist, it is ensured that the gate moves down of its own weight. The gates shall also go up and down without uneven pull to the gate, The winding of rope over the drum is uniform and according to the design. 3.9 Tn case of hydraulic hoists, it should be ensured that oil pressures are within the designed limits. 3.10 The full load current required for movement of the gate on load shall be measured and checked against the designed value.

3.11 When the rainy season starts. visual inspection of gates sh311 be made and they shall be lowered and raised several times to make sure that everything is in order,
9

IS. 10096 ( Part 2 ) - 1983
3.12 When the water starts overflowing, lower the gates to hold the water to half the height of gates In this position the seals may be tested and any leakage shall be attended to The gate. may also be operated up and down with this water load and operation of hoist shall be observed 3.13 The gates shall also be tested in a similar way against full water load. 3.14 During the testmg of gate ID dry condition ( see 3.1 to 3.9 ) and under water pressure, the following observations shall be made and a record be kept: a) Movement of gate and indication of jamming, if any; b) Effective stop is achieved by the gate stops wherever provided; c) Speed of opening and closing, and the current requirement at specified voltage, d) Operation of brakes and limit switches; e) Manual operauon of gate, if provided; f) Efficiency of guide rollers to check the side sway of the gate; g) Correctness of indrcation by local position indicators; hl Synchromzauon of remote position indicators, if provided; aod j) Vibrauon of gate, hoist, and civrl structure.
